Patient 1: [redacted name], Female

Patient 2: [redacted name], Male
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]

Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Inheritance study following abnormal findings in previous pregnancy loss. Previous pregnancy had trisomy 13 detected by PCR of placental material.

TEST PERFORMED
Targeted G-band karyotype analysis of chromosome 13

METHODOLOGY
Peripheral blood samples were collected from both partners. Lymphocytes were cultured and harvested according to standard protocols. G-banding was performed at 550-band resolution with targeted analysis of chromosome 13. A minimum of 20 metaphases were analyzed for each patient.

RESULTS

Patient 1 (Female): 46,XX
Targeted analysis of chromosome 13: Normal
No structural abnormalities or rearrangements detected

Patient 2 (Male): 46,XY
Targeted analysis of chromosome 13: Normal
No structural abnormalities or rearrangements detected

INTERPRETATION
No abnormality detected in chromosome 13 for either partner. Targeted analysis showed normal chromosome structure with no rearrangements. Neither partner has a chromosome rearrangement associated with the trisomy 13 found in the previous pregnancy loss.

The absence of structural chromosome 13 abnormalities in both parents suggests the previous trisomy 13 was likely due to nondisjunction during meiosis rather than an inherited chromosomal rearrangement. While no structural predisposition was identified, there remains an increased risk of trisomy 13 in future pregnancies compared to the general population.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Biochemical screening (first trimester combined screening or second trimester quad screen) for future pregnancies
2. Detailed ultrasound monitoring throughout pregnancy
3. Prenatal diagnosis (chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis) is available if needed
4. Genetic counseling to discuss recurrence risks and reproductive options

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
